latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Total clonal lymphoid proliferation across nodal/extranodal sites; primary upstream driver of paraneoplastic cytokine release, marrow/visceral infiltration, LDH elevation, and B symptoms.
IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β release from Reed-Sternberg cells (HL) or aggressive NHL cells; drives fever (including Pel-Ebstein pattern), night sweats, weight loss, anorexia.
Reactive hepatocyte acute-phase synthesis driving CRP, ESR, ferritin elevation, hypoalbuminemia, reactive thrombocytosis early then thrombocytopenia later.
Direct displacement of normal hematopoiesis by lymphoma cells (more typical of NHL than HL); drives multilineage cytopenias, leukoerythroblastic picture.
Active EBV in tumor cells (classical HL ~40%, NK/T-cell, post-transplant LPD, EBV+ DLBCL, Burkitt subset); also key trigger for secondary HLH; serum/whole-blood EBV DNA elevated.
Failure of NK / cytotoxic T cells to clear infected or malignant cells, sustaining IFN-γ output; central HLH defect; drives sIL-2R rise and low NK function.
Hyperactive IFN-γ → CXCL9/CXCL10 surge; signature axis of HLH; drives macrophage hyperactivation and sIL-2R elevation.
IFN-γ-driven macrophage hyperactivation with phagocytosis of hematopoietic cells; explains hyperferritinemia, hypofibrinogenemia, hypertriglyceridemia, cytopenias, hemophagocytosis on marrow.
Inflammasome-driven cytokine output amplifying fever and macrophage activation; particularly relevant when secondary HLH overlaps with autoinflammatory states.
Diffuse cytokine- and infiltration-driven liver and spleen inflammation; transaminitis, cholestasis, hepatosplenomegaly.
Spontaneous or therapy-induced cell turnover (especially Burkitt, lymphoblastic lymphoma, bulky DLBCL) → hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, AKI, marked LDH rise.
Cellular and humoral immune dysfunction (especially in HL and indolent NHL); predisposes to opportunistic infection that confounds the fever picture.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Tumor cells (Reed-Sternberg, activated B/T cells) constitutively secrete IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β driving B symptoms.
Direct nodal infiltration produces palpable, often painless lymphadenopathy (cervical, axillary, mediastinal, retroperitoneal).
Splenic infiltration (~30–40% of HL, >50% of advanced NHL) produces splenomegaly and hypersplenism.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: more common in advanced NHL, EBV+ disease, hepatic infiltration
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Hepatic sinusoidal/portal infiltration drives hepatomegaly and abnormal LFTs.
Cell turnover and tumor mass directly elevate LDH; LDH is in IPI/aaIPI prognostic scores.
Activated lymphocytes shed sCD25; markedly elevated in T-cell lymphoma, ATL, HL, secondary HLH; useful biomarker.
Cytokine-driven cachexia and anorexia produce >10% body weight loss over 6 months (B symptom criterion).
IL-1, IL-6, TNF act on hypothalamic PGE2 to produce neoplastic fever; classical Pel-Ebstein cyclic fever in HL.
Defervescence-associated drenching night sweats are a defining B symptom.
Cytokine-driven sickness behavior plus anemia produce profound fatigue.
IL-6 is the proximate driver of the hepatic acute-phase response.
Hepatocyte CRP synthesis is IL-6 dependent.
Fibrinogen and immunoglobulin elevation increase ESR; ESR is a prognostic factor in early-stage HL.
Negative acute-phase reactant; hypoalbuminemia <4 g/dL is a Hasenclever IPS prognostic factor for HL.
Anemia of chronic inflammation via hepcidin-mediated iron sequestration (IL-6 driven).
Acute-phase ferritin rise; markedly amplified when macrophage activation supervenes.
Marrow displacement causes normocytic anemia, sometimes with leukoerythroblastic picture.
Megakaryocyte loss and hypersplenism reduce platelet counts.
Granulocyte production impaired; deepens with chemotherapy.
EBV-driven tumors and immunosuppression sustain detectable plasma EBV DNA, often correlating with disease activity in EBV+ DLBCL, HL, NK/T-cell lymphoma, PTLD.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: especially T/NK lymphomas, EBV+ aggressive NHL, post-transplant
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: EBV-infected lymphocytes resist clearance, fueling chronic IFN-γ production and predisposing to lymphoma-associated HLH.
Sustained antigen presentation drives unrestrained IFN-γ from T/NK cells (canonical HLH cascade).
Functional NK cytotoxicity is reduced (HLH-2004 criterion).
Persistent T-cell activation increases sCD25 shedding; HLH-2004 criterion (>2400 U/mL).
CXCL9 is an IFN-γ-induced chemokine, used as a sensitive biomarker of active HLH.
IFN-γ is the dominant macrophage activator in HLH pathogenesis.
Hyperactivated macrophages release ferritin; >500 ng/mL is HLH-2004 criterion, >10000 ng/mL highly specific.
Glycosylated fraction <20% supports macrophage-activation states (AOSD/HLH); newer marker, less universally available.
TNF-α-mediated lipoprotein lipase suppression; >265 mg/dL is HLH-2004 criterion.
Plasmin activation by tPA from macrophages consumes fibrinogen; <150 mg/dL is HLH-2004 criterion (paradoxical given acute-phase nature).
Hemophagocytosis and consumption produce thrombocytopenia (HLH-2004: <100×10^9/L).
Hemophagocytosis-driven anemia; HLH-2004: hemoglobin <9 g/dL.
Hemophagocytosis of granulocyte precursors causes neutropenia (HLH-2004: ANC <1.0×10^9/L).
Marrow biopsy shows hemophagocytosis (presence supports HLH but absence does not exclude it).
Activated macrophages amplify hepatic and splenic inflammation.
Lymphoma-associated HLH carries 50–75% mortality without specific therapy; T/NK and EBV+ B-cell lymphomas highest risk.
IL-1/IL-18 are potent pyrogens, contributing to high spiking fevers in lymphoma-HLH.
Hepatocyte injury from cytokine storm and lymphomatous infiltration.
Often AST > ALT in HLH/MAS-driven hepatic injury.
Cholestasis and hemolysis raise bilirubin; jaundice in advanced disease.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: rare; intravascular T-cell lymphoma, EBV+ DLBCL with hepatic infiltration, HLH
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Hepatic lymphomatous infiltration with HLH can progress to liver failure.
Massive cell turnover sharply elevates LDH (often >2× baseline).
Uric-acid and calcium-phosphate crystal nephropathy → AKI.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: high-grade NHL, Burkitt, lymphoblastic, bulky disease, pre-treatment elevated LDH/uric acid
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Tumor lysis is a leading early cause of AKI in aggressive lymphoma.
Cellular immunodeficiency (especially HL and post-rituximab/post-chemo) raises bacterial, fungal, viral (PJP, VZV, CMV, EBV) infection risk.
Concurrent infection can drive much of the fever signal, making sepsis vs neoplastic fever vs HLH a key differential.
Lymphoma-associated HLH is the dominant proximate cause of early death; untreated mortality 50–75%.
TLS-associated AKI, dialysis dependence, and treatment delay raise short-term mortality.
Neutropenic and opportunistic infections are major mortality contributors during cytotoxic therapy.
Direct progression of refractory disease drives late mortality; histology and stage dependent.

axes.shape_free_text: Persistent low-grade to high spiking fever; classical Pel-Ebstein cyclic pattern (1–2 weeks fever alternating with afebrile periods) in HL; daily quotidian spikes when HLH supervenes. Often unresponsive to empiric antibiotics.
Painless, firm, often >2 cm lymph nodes (cervical, supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal, retroperitoneal). Bulky disease (>10 cm) carries prognostic weight.
Palpable spleen below costal margin, occasionally massive in indolent lymphomas, hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma, or HLH.
Smooth liver enlargement; more often in advanced/aggressive NHL and HLH.
Unintentional weight loss (>10% in 6 months defines a B symptom).
Drenching night sweats typically requiring change of clothes/bedding; classical B symptom.
Progressive disabling fatigue, often the dominant symptom outside fever spikes.
Generalized pruritus, sometimes severe; characteristic of HL but also NHL and Sézary syndrome.
Tracks fever; sinus tachycardia, often disproportionate when HLH or anemia present.
Elevation tracks tumor burden; markedly elevated in aggressive NHL, HLH, and tumor lysis.
Elevated in active lymphoma; >2400 U/mL in HLH; >5×10^4 U/mL very suggestive of lymphoma-HLH; correlates with disease activity and is used clinically in Japan as a lymphoma biomarker.
Modest elevation in lymphoma alone; markedly elevated (often >10000) when HLH supervenes.
Lower than normal in macrophage-activation states (HLH/AOSD/Still); typically <0.20 in active disease.
Elevated; frequently overlapping with infection range. Persistent elevation despite empiric antibiotics is a red flag for occult lymphoma.
Frequently very elevated (>50 mm/hr); ESR >50 is a Hasenclever/EORTC prognostic factor for HL.
Normocytic normochromic anemia of chronic inflammation; profound when marrow infiltration or HLH coexists. Hgb <10.5 g/dL in HL is a Hasenclever IPS factor.
Initially normal or reactive thrombocytosis; thrombocytopenia when marrow involvement or HLH supervenes.
Variable: neutrophilic leukocytosis in HL B-symptomatic disease, neutropenia with marrow infiltration or HLH.
Often normal or slightly elevated; lymphocyte-predominant elevation in CLL/SLL; circulating cells in leukemic-phase NHL. WBC ≥15000 is a Hasenclever IPS factor for HL.
Mild-moderate transaminase elevation typical; severe in HLH, hepatic infiltration, or hepatitis reactivation.
Tracks ALT; in HLH AST often > ALT.
Mildly elevated; jaundice in advanced disease, hepatic infiltration, or HLH-driven cholestasis.
Decreased; <4 g/dL is a Hasenclever IPS factor.
Elevated when HLH active; >265 mg/dL meets HLH-2004.
Initially elevated as acute-phase reactant, then paradoxically decreased in HLH (<150 mg/dL).
Reduced or absent in active HLH (HLH-2004 criterion).
IFN-γ-induced; sensitive HLH biomarker, more dynamic than ferritin in some series.
Hemophagocytic histiocytes ingesting RBCs/platelets/neutrophils on marrow biopsy; supportive but not required for HLH diagnosis.
Elevated in EBV+ lymphomas (HL, EBV+ DLBCL, NK/T-cell, PTLD); can be exceedingly high (>10^6) in EBV-driven HLH.
Elevated by tumor lysis, ureteral obstruction from bulky retroperitoneal nodes, or pre-renal volume depletion.
Markedly elevated in tumor lysis (often >8 mg/dL); precipitates in renal tubules.
Hypercalcemia of malignancy in some lymphomas (ATL/HTLV-1, B-cell with 1,25-OH-D production); hypocalcemia in tumor lysis.
axes.second_peak: Hypocalcemia (5.5–8.0 mg/dL) during tumor lysis from calcium-phosphate precipitation, days 0–7.

axes.shape_free_text: Derived ratio LDH / upper-limit-of-normal LDH; >1 used in IPI scoring; >2 suggests aggressive disease or HLH.
Probability that lymphoma is the underlying driver of fever in an FUO workup; integrates B symptoms, LDH, sIL-2R, lymphadenopathy, imaging.
Bayesian confidence that HLH-2004 / HScore criteria are met; thresholding informs urgency of HLH-directed therapy.
Risk of HBV reactivation with rituximab and other B-cell-depleting or chemo regimens; HBsAg+, anti-HBc+ patients especially.
Probability that ongoing infection is a major contributor to fever rather than (or in addition to) lymphoma; raises bar for stopping antibiotics.
Smoldering macrophage activation pressure short of full HLH; predicts decompensation under steroids alone or chemotherapy initiation.
Daily hazard of fulminant HLH/MAS development; markedly elevated in T/NK-cell lymphomas, EBV+ aggressive B-cell lymphoma, advanced disease.
Daily hazard of AKI from tumor lysis, obstruction, sepsis, drug nephrotoxicity.
Daily hazard of bacterial/fungal/viral infection; baseline raised by lymphoma immunodeficiency, dramatically raised during chemotherapy-induced neutropenia.
Daily hazard of acute liver failure from hepatic infiltration, HLH, or HBV reactivation.
Composite mortality hazard incorporating HLH, AKI, sepsis, and refractory disease pathways. Untreated lymphoma-HLH mortality 50–75%; aggressive NHL 5-year overall survival 50–70% depending on IPI.

axis_couplings.conditionality: high-grade NHL, bulky disease, around treatment initiation
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Both reflect cell turnover; jointly elevated in tumor lysis.
Paradoxical decoupling of acute-phase reactants is a hallmark of HLH.

axis_couplings.conditionality: in lymphoma without infection, PCT often disproportionately low for CRP/fever
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: PCT helps discriminate neoplastic fever (low PCT) from bacterial sepsis (high PCT) when CRP is similarly elevated.
EBV burden tracks T-cell activation in EBV-driven disease.
Both track total tumor burden and stage III/IV disease.
HLH-driven shock and rhabdomyolysis-like myocardial/hepatic injury propagate to kidney.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Excisional or core-needle biopsy of an accessible peripheral or deep node is the single most important diagnostic step; FNA alone is generally inadequate for lymphoma classification.

side_effects.interpretation: Generally low risk for peripheral nodes; higher for mediastinal/retroperitoneal cores.

treatments.context_specific_role: Establishing histologic diagnosis and subtype; bone marrow biopsy is complementary for staging and HLH workup.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: When occult infection is plausible (especially neutropenic fever), empiric antibiotics shorten febrile period if infection is contributing.
Antibiotics do not affect neoplastic fever; persistent fever despite adequate empiric coverage is a key clue to lymphoma.

side_effects.interpretation: C. difficile risk rises with prolonged broad-spectrum exposure.

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard FUO/sepsis pathway; should not delay biopsy and HLH workup once lymphoma is suspected.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Naproxen test (Chang test): rapid, complete defervescence supports neoplastic fever (classically HL). Limited specificity but historically used.

failure_modes: false-positive in adult Still's, other inflammatory states

side_effects.interpretation: NSAID-induced AKI risk especially with hypovolemia or TLS.

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunctive diagnostic clue when imaging/histology pending; not a substitute for biopsy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Dexamethasone (HLH-94/HLH-2004) suppresses cytokine storm and macrophage activation, controlling fever and ferritin.
If active untreated infection drives the picture, steroids without antimicrobials worsen outcome.
Pre-biopsy steroids can render lymph node histology non-diagnostic and trigger TLS in chemo-sensitive lymphoma; obtain tissue first whenever feasible.

failure_modes: precipitates TLS in highly chemo-sensitive lymphoma
treatments.context_specific_role: Bridge while definitive lymphoma therapy is organized, especially when HLH features dominate; ideally given after tissue diagnosis.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HLH-94/HLH-2004 backbone for lymphoma-HLH; depletes activated T cells/macrophages.
Profound cytopenias may force dose reduction.

treatments.context_specific_role: Cornerstone for HLH-directed therapy in lymphoma-HLH; usually as part of HLH-94 protocol or DEP/CHOEP-like regimens, then transition to definitive lymphoma chemotherapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Standard frontline for CD20+ aggressive B-NHL (DLBCL, certain follicular grades, MCL with modifications); requires confirmed histology.
Rituximab can precipitate fulminant HBV reactivation; entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis required for HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients.

side_effects.interpretation: Febrile neutropenia common; G-CSF support required.

treatments.context_specific_role: Definitive cytotoxic regimen for aggressive B-cell NHL once histology is established and HLH (if present) has been bridged; Pola-R-CHP is an emerging alternative for high-IPI DLBCL.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Standard frontline for classical HL; A+AVD (brentuximab vedotin substituting bleomycin) increasingly preferred for advanced HL.

side_effects.interpretation: Bleomycin pneumonitis risk; monitor PFTs and DLCO.

treatments.context_specific_role: Definitive frontline for classical HL after biopsy and PET staging.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Anti-HBV nucleos(t)ide prophylaxis mandatory in HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: Backbone of CD20+ B-NHL therapy; combined with chemotherapy in aggressive disease, can be monotherapy bridge in frail patients.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Bulky aggressive NHL/Burkitt/lymphoblastic mandate rasburicase (or allopurinol for low-risk) before cytotoxic therapy.
Rasburicase is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency due to severe hemolysis risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Pre-treatment phase for aggressive lymphoma to prevent TLS-related AKI.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High-volume isotonic crystalloid (~3 L/m²/day) improves tubular flow and reduces uric acid/phosphate crystal deposition.

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard component of TLS prevention bundle.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Entecavir or tenofovir for HBsAg+ patients receiving rituximab/anti-CD20 or B-cell-depleting therapy; consider for anti-HBc+ patients per local guidelines.

treatments.context_specific_role: Mandatory adjunct to immunochemotherapy in HBV-exposed patients, continued ≥6–12 months after therapy completion.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: PJP prophylaxis recommended during fludarabine, alemtuzumab, prolonged steroids, certain regimens (e.g., escalated BEACOPP), and in HIV-coinfected lymphoma.

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard prophylaxis during T-cell-depleting or steroid-heavy lymphoma regimens.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Primary or secondary prophylaxis for high-risk regimens (R-CHOP-21 in elderly, dose-dense regimens).

failure_modes: may aggravate HLH cytokine storm in active MAS-HLH
treatments.context_specific_role: Reduces febrile-neutropenia risk during chemotherapy cycles.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Anakinra used off-label in MAS/secondary HLH especially with prominent IL-1/IL-18 signature; favorable safety in critically ill.

failure_modes: incomplete response in IFN-γ-dominant HLH (consider emapalumab)
treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunct in steroid-refractory secondary HLH, often combined with HLH-directed therapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Ruxolitinib blocks JAK-STAT signaling downstream of IFN-γ and other γc cytokines; emerging data in malignancy-associated HLH.

treatments.context_specific_role: Salvage option for refractory secondary HLH; bridge to definitive lymphoma therapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: CNS prophylaxis (IT methotrexate ± high-dose MTX) for high CNS-IPI DLBCL, Burkitt, lymphoblastic lymphoma, testicular DLBCL.

treatments.context_specific_role: Selected high-risk subtypes for CNS relapse prevention.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Standard salvage for relapsed/refractory chemosensitive aggressive NHL and HL; CAR-T increasingly used in r/r DLBCL.
Axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, tisagenlecleucel for r/r large B-cell lymphoma; second-line vs ASCT in chemorefractory patients.

side_effects.interpretation: CRS-related fever, often confused with infection.

treatments.context_specific_role: Approved for r/r LBCL after ≥1 (selected) or ≥2 prior therapies; CRS overlaps clinically with HLH.

young_adult_15_35.trajectory_modulation: First peak of bimodal HL incidence; mediastinal nodular sclerosing HL most common.

elderly_above_60.trajectory_modulation: Most NHL incidence; second HL peak; worse tolerance of chemotherapy; higher risk of treatment-related mortality.

ebv_associated.trajectory_modulation: Drives EBV+ HL, EBV+ DLBCL, NK/T-cell lymphoma, Burkitt (endemic), PTLD; raises HLH risk.

uncontrolled_hiv.trajectory_modulation: Markedly raises risk of aggressive NHL (DLBCL, Burkitt, primary CNS lymphoma, plasmablastic) and HL; often EBV-driven.

post_transplant_or_chronic_immunosuppres.trajectory_modulation: PTLD risk; methotrexate-associated lymphoproliferative disease; thiopurine + anti-TNF lymphoma risk.

sjogren_or_ra_or_celiac.trajectory_modulation: Sjögren → MALT/parotid lymphoma; celiac → enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma (EATL); RA → DLBCL.

htlv1_seropositive.trajectory_modulation: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL) risk in HTLV-1 carriers, endemic in southwestern Japan, Caribbean, parts of Africa; presents with hypercalcemia, lymphadenopathy, skin lesions.

chronic_hcv.trajectory_modulation: Marginal-zone lymphoma (splenic, MALT) and DLBCL risk; HCV eradication can induce indolent lymphoma regression.

chronic_gastric_infection.trajectory_modulation: Gastric MALT lymphoma; eradication therapy curative in early-stage disease.

first_degree_relative.trajectory_modulation: Modest familial risk; specific syndromes (XLP, ALPS) drive HLH/lymphoma risk.

perforin_unc13d_xlp_or_others.trajectory_modulation: Familial HLH syndromes predispose to lymphoma and severe HLH; relevant in pediatric/young adult presentations of lymphoma-fever.

supportive_care: Excisional or generous core lymph node biopsy first whenever feasible — avoid empiric high-dose steroids before tissue diagnosis as they obscure histology and can precipitate TLS.

Concurrent bone marrow aspirate and biopsy when fever is unexplained, cytopenias are present, or HLH is suspected; flow cytometry, IHC, EBER in situ hybridization, T-cell receptor / IGH clonality, and cytogenetics.
Comprehensive HLH workup: ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, sIL-2R, NK function, CXCL9 if available, EBV/CMV PCR; calculate HScore and apply HLH-2004 criteria.

Tumor lysis risk stratification (Cairo-Bishop) and pre-emptive bundle: vigorous IV hydration, allopurinol for low-intermediate risk, rasburicase for high-risk (after G6PD screening), strict electrolyte and renal monitoring.
Hepatitis B serology (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs) and HBV-DNA in all patients before anti-CD20; entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis for HBsAg+ and individualized prophylaxis/monitoring for anti-HBc+.
HIV testing in all newly diagnosed lymphoma patients; HCV testing especially in marginal-zone or DLBCL.
Latent TB screening (IGRA) before high-dose steroids or biologics; consider strongyloides serology for endemic regions.
PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX or alternatives) during prolonged steroid or T-cell-depleting therapy; antiviral (acyclovir/valacyclovir) and antifungal prophylaxis tailored to regimen and ANC nadir risk.
Vaccination: assess and update inactivated vaccinations before therapy; avoid live vaccines during and ≥6 months after treatment; influenza and pneumococcal vaccination encouraged.
Fertility preservation counseling (sperm banking, oocyte/embryo cryopreservation, GnRH-agonist) before gonadotoxic regimens, especially in young adults with HL.
Cardiology baseline (echocardiogram, ECG) before anthracycline-containing regimens; consider dexrazoxane in selected high cumulative-dose situations.
Pulmonary function testing including DLCO before bleomycin-containing therapy; monitor for bleomycin pneumonitis with new dyspnea or hypoxemia.
Antiemetic prophylaxis (5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone ± NK1 antagonist) per emetogenicity classification.
G-CSF primary prophylaxis for high-risk regimens (R-CHOP-21 in elderly, dose-dense regimens, prior febrile neutropenia).
Pain control with WHO ladder; avoid IM injections in thrombocytopenia; care with NSAIDs in renal impairment / TLS risk.
Nutritional assessment and intervention; cachexia is common and adds chemotherapy intolerance.
Multidisciplinary input: hematology-oncology, infectious disease (FUO/HLH co-management), hepatology if hepatic involvement, transplant team early in high-risk relapse settings.
Psychological support and adequate explanation in the patient's language; involve palliative care for symptom management even during curative intent therapy.
Clear, written instructions on febrile neutropenia precautions: when to present to hospital, avoidance of high-risk foods, hand hygiene, household exposure precautions.
Documentation of advance care planning early, particularly in elderly or refractory disease.
